report:
Fresh complete followup assessment of meta.reviews.review_instructions. Saved and read prior inputs/report before start; recaptured the fixture and full review-design dependencies and compared all fragments. The only change is a placeholder_status association comment before test inventory construction in review.rs. The full claim, main.rs, both annotated tests, fixture helpers and design context are unchanged. No instruction handling behavior changed.

The complete claim requires exact preservation of the verification prompt and all additional coordinator instructions as recorded context, including instructions which do not originate in a source file. Both ordinary implementation associations remain sufficient. inventory constructs ReviewInput.prompt directly from PROMPT. review::start accepts owned Vec<String>, assigns it directly to coordinator_instructions, serializes the complete input to input.json and returns that input; there is no trimming, reordering or source-file requirement. The CLI review handler reads an optional instructions file with read_to_string and forwards its unchanged contents as one vector element, while no-instruction startup passes an empty vector. The output shown to the reviewer serializes the same returned input. capture_read appends fragments without replacing these context fields; recording consumes the saved input and writes output/summary rather than rewriting the context. The new status marker does not intersect these paths.

Both associated tests were read fully. initial_context_preserves_instructions_and_exact_uniform_fragments supplies two runtime strings directly, including an embedded newline, asserts exact instruction-vector equality and order, exact prompt equality with PROMPT, and equality between returned and deserialized persisted input. This exercises the non-source instruction case and detects normalization, loss or reordering. Its source-fragment assertions show context coexists with actual captured source. cli_start_and_record_roundtrip_exact_saved_input writes multiline instructions, invokes the actual executable with --instructions, requires successful startup and exact stdout/persisted-input equality, and asserts the precise instruction string including newline. It then records a report, requires success/check acceptance and rejects malformed record invocation. The captured Fixture helper constructs actual files and invokes the real executable; its input helper deserializes input.json, so equality is not tautological. There are no TODO/N/A implementation or test entries and no deferred requirement.

The comment-only delta was checked against the full prior assessment and all current claim aspects; no other relied-on inputs changed. This is source assessment with fresh start/read/record, not claimed test execution. No source edits or test-suite reruns were performed, and no requested edits remain.
